speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: MTI has several strategies to develop a vibrant ecosystem for business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: First, we are looking at ways to grow our economy and enable companies to seize new opportunities, both locally and overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This includes transforming our industries, developing new sectors, such as agri-tech and precision medicine, and supporting our companies to tap on external growth opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Second, we are fostering a pro-enterprise environment by lowering the barriers of entry and exit for businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Businesses can also benefit from lower licence fees and quicker processing time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We will extend this to other sectors, such as retail and environmental services, so that more businesses can benefit from the rules review and process re-engineering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These include Startup SG Founder, which provides mentorship and startup capital grants to first-time entrepreneurs with innovative business ideas and Startup SG Network, which connects startup ecosystem players.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: To succeed in our goal of building a vibrant business ecosystem, we need a collective effort from business owners, workers and the Government to work in partnership to transform our economy and enterprises together.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In relation to the continued level of "healthy" cessation of businesses, as stated in the last part of my original question, can the Senior Minister of State share whether MTI has any specific level of target in terms of the definition of "healthy" cessation of businesses?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In relation to the economic cycle we are facing now, whether there is any good feel of "healthy" cessation of businesses going forward, in taking into particular consideration, the outlook of the economy.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is part and parcel of a well-functioning economy.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: What we want is to ensure that, in the end, resources are being channelled into the more productive, more competitive firms.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Over time, if we do this well, then the economy will get stronger and stronger, the capabilities in our enterprises will get stronger and our workers will be able to get better jobs.
